mainTopic: An agent who misreports the wife's instructions, when a husband can retract a גט given to an agent, and whether 'here you are' counts like 'acquire'
overview: First the גמרא shows that רב נחמן's ruling about an agent who misreported the wife's words proves nothing about whose words the husband relies on. In his case, the agent cancelled his own agency by saying he would only receive the גט. רב הונא בר חייא and then רבא challenge רב נחמן with two sources. One is a husband who says 'receive this גט for my wife.' The other is a קטנה who appoints a receiving agent. In both, the husband seems to want her divorced in any way that works. The גמרא answers that in those cases the husband knowingly meant delivery, while in רב נחמן's case he was fooled. A ברייתא about switched wording is read so that it does not clash with רב נחמן. That ברייתא shows the husband can rely on the agent's words, but רב נחמן's case differs because the husband said 'here you are, as she said.' Next comes a ברייתא with three views on when a husband can take back a גט given to the wife's receiving agent: the first opinion, רבי נתן, and רבי. Finally the גמרא asks whether, for רבי נתן, 'here you are' counts like 'acquire,' and begins quoting a משנה to answer. The answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If the case were reversed, we could learn something
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to push away the proof from רב נחמן's ruling. It describes a reversed case where a conclusion really could be drawn.
steps.simpleTranslation: It would make sense to learn something if the opposite case had been stated. Suppose she said 'receive my גט for me,' and the agent told the husband 'your wife said bring me my גט.' The husband answered 'here it is, as she said,' and רב נחמן ruled that once the גט reaches the agent's hand she is divorced. That would show the husband relies on her words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a rejection of the earlier proof. It describes a made-up reversed case where we really could tell whose words the husband relies on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the reversed case, the wife made the agent an agent for receiving. If she were divorced as soon as the agent got the גט, that could only be because the husband went along with her version. So a ruling like that would prove he relies on her words. The point is that the real case does not work this way, and that comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It would make sense if… (opens a contrast with the real case)
the opposite / reversed
receive my גט for me (agent for receiving)
bring me my גט (agent for bringing)
he relies on her words

steps.confusionAlert: This whole step is a hypothetical. The real ruling of רב נחמן was about the opposite wording, and there she was NOT divorced.

phrases.english: It would be understandable if the opposite had been stated:
[she said:] "Receive my bill of divorce for me,"
and [the agent said:] "Your wife said: Bring me my bill of divorce,"
and he [the husband] says: "Here it is, as she said";

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: and Rav Nachman said that Rabba bar Avuh said that Rav said:
once the bill of divorce reached his [the agent's] hand, she is divorced —

phrases.aramaic: אַלְמָא אַדִּיבּוּרָא דִידַהּ הוּא דְּקָא סָמֵיךְ;
phrases.english: that would show it is on her words that he relies;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins rejecting the attempt, made before this section, to learn from רב נחמן's ruling whose words the husband relies on.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference drawn from רב נחמן's actual ruling.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Only a ruling in a different case (reversed wording, or 'her hand') would show whose words he relies on.

steps.title: In the real case, the agent cancelled his own agency
steps.stepSummary: Or, if the ruling had said 'her hand,' we would learn he relies on the agent's words. But in the actual case she is not divorced because the agent cancelled his role completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or, if רב נחמן had said 'once it reached her hand,' that would show the husband relies on the agent's words. But here the real reason is different: the agent uprooted his agency completely. He said 'I am an agent for receiving, not for delivering.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes pushing away the proof. It gives the real reason she is not divorced in רב נחמן's case, and that reason has nothing to do with whose words the husband relies on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The agent said 'your wife told me to receive it,' and that means 'I am not taking on the job of delivering.' So he is not the husband's agent for delivery. He is also not truly the wife's agent for receiving, because she only asked him to bring it. Since he is nobody's agent, she is not divorced, and the case proves nothing about whose words the husband relies on.

keyTerms.meaning: or else / alternatively
he uprooted (cancelled) his own agency
agent for receiving (acts for the wife)
agent for delivering (acts for the husband)

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן's case teaches nothing about whose words the husband relies on. She is not divorced because the agent, by calling himself only a receiver, made himself nobody's agent.

phrases.english: Or else, if he had said "[once it reaches] her hand" —
that would show he relies on his [the agent's] words.
But here —

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּעַקְרַיהּ שָׁלִיחַ לִשְׁלִיחוּתֵיהּ לִגְמָרֵי הוּא;
phrases.english: it is because the agent uprooted his agency completely;
for he said: I am an agent for receiving,
for delivering I am not.
phrases.notes: In other words, he is telling the husband he won't take on the job of bringing it to her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָכָא מִשּׁוּם דְּעַקְרַיהּ שָׁלִיחַ לִשְׁלִיחוּתֵיהּ לִגְמָרֵי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the rejection begun in step 1 by giving the real reason for רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב נחמן's ruling shows whose words the husband relies on.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is not divorced because the agent cancelled his agency completely. This has nothing to do with whose words the husband relies on.

steps.title: רב הונא בר חייא cites a משנה: the husband may retract
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חייא quotes a משנה: a husband who says 'receive' or 'deliver this גט for my wife' may retract. He infers that if the husband does not retract, it is a valid גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חייא said: Come hear a source. If someone says 'receive this גט for my wife' or 'deliver this גט to my wife,' and he wants to take it back, he may. The only reason it fails is that he wanted to take it back. If he did not want to, it is a valid גט.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר חייא starts a challenge against רב נחמן. He quotes a משנה and draws an inference from it. The punch of the challenge comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets the husband retract in both wordings. The inference is that without a retraction, even the 'receive' wording produces a valid גט. That is surprising, and the next step uses it against רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: come and hear (introduces a source)
if he wants to retract, he may retract
the reason is…, but otherwise… (an inference from the wording)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא: תָּא שְׁמַע,
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chiyya said: Come and hear:
One who says: "Receive this bill of divorce for my wife"
or "Deliver this bill of divorce to my wife,"
if he wishes to retract, he may retract.
The reason [it fails] is that he wished [to retract];
but if he did not wish to, it is a valid bill of divorce;

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִיָּיא: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the earlier proof is pushed away, a new challenge against רב נחמן's ruling begins.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that she is not divorced
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה implies that a husband's 'receive' wording still produces a valid גט. This is set up here and completed in step 4.

steps.title: He wants her divorced in any way that works
steps.stepSummary: A husband cannot appoint an agent for receiving, yet the משנה's גט works. That must be because he wants her divorced in any valid way. The same should apply in רב נחמן's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why should that be a valid גט? A husband cannot appoint an agent for receiving! So we must say that since he made up his mind to divorce her, he means 'let her be divorced in whatever way works.' Here too, in רב נחמן's case, since he made up his mind to divorce her, he means 'let her be divorced in whatever way works.'
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge reaches its punch line. The idea that explains the משנה should also make the wife divorced in רב נחמן's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the wife can make someone an agent for receiving. So the husband's 'receive' wording should mean nothing. The משנה still counts it, so the husband's real wish must be 'divorce her however it works,' and the agent acts as a delivery agent. Applied to רב נחמן's case, the husband who said 'here it is, as she said' also wants her divorced, so once the גט reaches her she should be divorced.

keyTerms.meaning: but why?
not able to appoint
he made up his mind to divorce her
in whatever way she can be divorced

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out a key idea: a husband who has decided to divorce wants the גט to work in any valid way. Wording that does not fit, like 'receive,' does not cancel his intent.

phrases.english: But why [is it a valid divorce]?

phrases.aramaic: הָא בַּעַל לָאו בַּר שַׁוּוֹיֵי שָׁלִיחַ לְִקַבָּלָה הוּא!
phrases.english: The husband is not able to appoint an agent for receiving!
Rather, we say:
since he has set his mind on divorcing her,

phrases.aramaic: מֵימָר אָמַר: תִּיגָּרַשׁ כֹּל הֵיכִי דְּמִגָּרְשָׁה;
phrases.english: he is saying: Let her be divorced in whatever way she becomes divorced;
here too [in רב נחמן's case],
since he has set his mind on divorcing her,

phrases.aramaic: מֵימָר אָמַר: תִּיגָּרַשׁ כֹּל הֵיכִי דְּמִגָּרְשָׁה!
phrases.english: he is saying: Let her be divorced in whatever way she becomes divorced!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? הָא בַּעַל לָאו בַּר שַׁוּוֹיֵי שָׁלִיחַ לְקַבָּלָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב הונא בר חייא's challenge by explaining the inference from the משנה and applying it to רב נחמן's case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that even when the גט reaches her hand she is not divorced
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The husband's intent to divorce 'in any way that works' turns the 'receive' wording into valid delivery. That same intent should make her divorced in רב נחמן's case.

steps.title: The husband knew he could not appoint a receiving agent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison to the משנה. There, the husband knew a receiving agent for him does not work, so he meant delivery. Here, the husband was misled.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare? There, a person knows there is no agency for receiving, so he made up his mind and gave it as delivery. Here, he is making a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the challenge from Step 4 by showing the two cases are different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, everyone knows a husband cannot appoint someone to receive the גט for his wife. So when he said 'receive,' he really meant 'deliver.' In רב נחמן's case, the agent lied and said the wife made him a receiving agent. The husband believed him, so he was relying on a mistake, not choosing delivery.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? (a phrase that rejects a comparison)
agency for receiving the גט on the wife's behalf
delivery: the agent carries the גט from the husband to the wife
he errs / is mistaken

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, a person knows
that there is no agency for receiving,
phrases.notes: He means the husband cannot appoint someone to receive for his wife. Only she can do that.

phrases.english: so he made up his mind and gave it for the sake of delivery;
here, he errs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קשיא of Steps 3-4
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the משנה of 'receive for my wife' and רב נחמן's case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In the משנה the husband knowingly chose delivery. In רב נחמן's case he was misled by the agent.

steps.title: רבא's challenge from a minor girl who appointed a receiving agent
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a משנה: a קטנה who told an agent 'receive my גט' is divorced once it reaches her hand, even though the husband never made him a delivery agent. So the husband wants her divorced any way possible, and the same should apply in רב נחמן's case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Come hear. A minor girl who said 'receive my גט for me,' it is not a גט until it reaches her hand. At least once it reaches her hand she is divorced. Why? He never made him a delivery agent! Rather, we say: since he decided to divorce her, he says 'let her be divorced any way she can be.' Here too, the same should be said.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a new source to challenge רב נחמן, using the same reasoning the גמרא used in Step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטנה cannot appoint an agent, so the agent's receiving does nothing for her. Yet when the גט reaches her hand she is divorced. That only works if the agent counts as the husband's delivery agent, which the husband never said outright. So the husband must want the divorce to work any way it can, and that should be true in רב נחמן's case too.

keyTerms.meaning: a minor girl
Come hear (introduces a source used as a proof)
he set his mind on divorcing her
in any way she can be divorced

phrases.english: Rava said: Come hear,
a minor girl who said:
'Receive my גט for me'
it is not a גט
until the גט reaches her hand.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מָטֵי גִּיטָּא לִידַהּ – מִיהָא מִגָּרְשָׁה,
phrases.english: When the גט reaches her hand, at least, she is divorced.
But why?
He did not make him an agent for delivery!
Rather, we say:
since he set his mind on divorcing her,
he says to himself:
'Let her be divorced in any way that she can be divorced';
here too,
phrases.notes: Here means רב נחמן's case of the agent who misreported her words.

phrases.english: since he set his mind on divorcing her,
he says to himself:
'Let her be divorced in any way that she can be divorced!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge built on the same reasoning as Step 4, from a different משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that she is not divorced even when the גט reaches her hand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The קטנה case shows a husband wants the divorce to work any way possible, even without saying 'deliver.' So in רב נחמן's case the agent should count as a delivery agent.

steps.title: The husband knew a minor cannot appoint an agent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's proof the same way. Everyone knows a קטנה cannot appoint an agent, so the husband knowingly gave it as his own delivery. Here, he was misled.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare? There, a person knows there is no agency for a minor, so he made up his mind and gave it to her as his own delivery. Here, he is making a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away רבא's challenge, using the same answer it gave in Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband knew the קטנה's appointment means nothing, so when he handed over the גט, he meant the agent to be his own delivery agent. In רב נחמן's case, the husband believed the agent's false claim, so his intent was built on a mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: a minor cannot appoint an agent
his own delivery: the agent acts for the husband

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There, a person knows
that there is no agency for a minor,
so he made up his mind and gave it to her
for the sake of his own delivery;
here, he errs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבא's challenge in Step 6
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the קטנה case and רב נחמן's case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: With a קטנה the husband knowingly chose delivery. In רב נחמן's case he was misled.
steps.whatToRemember: Both rejections (Steps 5 and 7) use the same idea. When the husband knows the receiving agency fails, he knowingly means delivery. When he is fooled by the agent, we cannot say that.

steps.title: A ברייתא about an agent who switched the wife's words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. Even when the agent changes 'bring' to 'receive' or the reverse, the husband may retract, but once the גט reaches her hand she is divorced. This looks like a direct challenge to רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: She said 'bring me my גט,' and he told the husband 'your wife said receive my גט for me.' Or she said 'receive my גט for me,' and he said 'your wife said bring me my גט.' And the husband says 'deliver and give it to her,' or 'acquire it for her,' or 'receive it for her.' If he wants to retract, he may retract. Once the גט reaches her hand, she is divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to describe exactly רב נחמן's case and reaches the opposite result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case in the ברייתא is רב נחמן's case: she said 'bring' and the agent told the husband 'receive.' Yet the ברייתא says she is divorced once the גט reaches her hand, while רב נחמן said she is not. The גמרא's response to this comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Bring me my גט (she is divorced only when it reaches her)
Receive my גט for me (she is divorced when the agent receives it)
acquire it for her
if he wants to retract, he may retract

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two kinds of agent straight. A delivery agent (הולכה) works for the husband, so the divorce happens when the גט reaches her hand. A receiving agent (קבלה) works for the wife, so the divorce happens as soon as the agent gets it.

phrases.english: Come hear:
She said 'Bring me my גט,'
and the agent told the husband 'Your wife said: Receive my גט for me';
or she said 'Receive my גט for me,'
and he said 'Your wife said: Bring me my גט,'
and the husband says: 'Deliver and give it to her,'
or 'Acquire it for her,' or 'Receive it for her'
if he wants to retract, he may retract;
once the גט reaches her hand, she is divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After two rejected comparisons, brings a ברייתא that seems to speak about רב נחמן's case directly
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that she is not divorced even when the גט reaches her hand
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא covers the case of 'bring' switched to 'receive' and rules she is divorced once the גט reaches her hand. That is the opposite of רב נחמן's ruling.
steps.whyThisMatters: Unlike the earlier sources, this ברייתא cannot be answered with 'there he knew, here he erred,' because it deals with the very same mistake.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא as the husband echoing the agent's words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא means the husband answered with the same language the agent used. That reading would contradict רב נחמן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't the ברייתא talking about a husband who answered 'receive' to the agent's 'receive', and 'bring' to the agent's 'bring'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains exactly how the ברייתא from step 8 challenges רב נחמן. It reads the ברייתא as a case where the husband simply repeated the agent's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the agent wrongly told the husband 'she said receive,' and the husband answered 'receive it for her.' That is just like רב נחמן's case. Yet the ברייתא says she is divorced once the גט reaches her hand, while רב נחמן says she is not divorced at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Receiving: the agent accepts the גט on the woman's behalf
Delivery: the agent carries the גט for the husband to the woman
'What, is it not...?' The גמרא proposes a reading of a source

phrases.english: What, is it not 'receive' in response to 'receive',
phrases.notes: The husband says 'receive' after the agent told him the wife said 'receive'.

phrases.english: and 'bring' in response to 'bring'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the reading of the ברייתא that makes step 8's challenge work
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling that she is not divorced when the agent misreported her words
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the husband echoed the agent's false words and she is still divorced, then רב נחמן's ruling is contradicted

steps.title: The husband's words matched what the wife really said
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: the husband answered with the opposite of the agent's claim, which matched the wife's actual words.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means the husband said 'receive' to the agent's 'bring', and 'bring' to the agent's 'receive'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the reading from step 9. It says the husband's words were the opposite of what the agent claimed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the agent switched the wife's words, a husband who says the opposite of the agent's claim is actually matching what the wife really said. That is why the ברייתא allows the divorce, and it no longer contradicts רב נחמן.

keyTerms.meaning: 'No': the גמרא rejects the suggested reading

phrases.english: No; 'receive' in response to 'bring',
and 'bring' in response to 'receive'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 9's reading of the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading that makes the ברייתא contradict רב נחמן
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as a case where the husband's words matched the wife's real words, which is not רב נחמן's case

steps.title: Why not divorced immediately? The husband relies on the agent's words
steps.stepSummary: If the wife really appointed a receiving agent and the husband said 'receive', the divorce should work as soon as the agent gets the גט. Since the ברייתא waits until it reaches her hand, the husband must be relying on what the agent told him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is 'receive' in response to 'bring', then as soon as the גט reaches the agent's hand it should be a valid גט right away! Learn from this that the husband relies on the agent's statement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not throw out the reading from step 10. It draws a consequence from it: since the divorce waits for her hand, the husband must go by what the agent told him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the 'receive' for 'bring' case, the wife really did appoint a receiving agent, and the husband said 'receive'. So the divorce should take effect the moment the agent holds the גט. The ברייתא says it only works in her hand, which shows the husband relied on the agent's word 'bring' and meant him as a delivery agent.

keyTerms.meaning: Immediately, right away
'Learn from this': drawing a conclusion
Speech, statement
Relies on

phrases.english: If it is 'receive' in response to 'bring',
from when the גט reaches his hand,
phrases.notes: 'His hand' means the agent's hand, not the wife's.

phrases.english: let it be a גט immediately!
Learn from this
that he relies on his statement!
phrases.notes: The husband relies on the agent's statement ('she said bring'), so he meant the agent to deliver.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי קַבָּלָה אַהוֹלָכָה מִכִּי מָטֵי גִּיטָּא לִידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 10's reading, then draws a conclusion from the ברייתא's ruling
steps.kashyaTarget: Whose words the husband relies on in רב נחמן's case, where he said 'here you are, as she said'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real receiving agent plus the husband saying 'receive' should make the divorce work at once. The ברייתא waits for her hand, so the husband must be relying on the agent's words. The גמרא wants to apply this to רב נחמן's case, and step 12 pushes that back.

steps.title: רב נחמן's case is different: 'here you are, as she said'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the two cases cannot be compared. In רב נחמן's case the husband said 'here you are, as she said', and in the ברייתא he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? There, he said to him: 'Here you are, as she said.' Here, did he say to him: 'Here you are, as she said'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא refuses to treat the ברייתא and רב נחמן's case as the same. It points to the husband's different words in each case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב נחמן's case the husband explicitly tied his act to 'as she said'. In the ברייתא he just handed over the גט, relying on the agent's statement. Because the husband's words are different, the ruling in one case says nothing about the other.

keyTerms.meaning: 'How can you compare?': rejecting a comparison
'Here you are, as she said'
There (the other case) / here (this case)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא works because the husband relied on the agent's statement. רב נחמן's case is different because the husband said 'here you are, as she said'.

phrases.english: How can you compare?!
There he said to him:
'Here you are, as she said,'
here, did he say to him:
'Here you are, as she said'?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects linking the conclusion of step 11 to רב נחמן's case
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the comparison between the ברייתא and רב נחמן's case
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The husband's words are different: only in רב נחמן's case did he say 'here you are, as she said'

steps.title: The first opinion: once the wife appointed a receiving agent, the husband cannot take it back
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: the wife appointed a שליח קבלה. Whether the husband says 'bring', 'give', 'acquire', or 'receive', he cannot retract once he hands over the גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The wife said to the agent, 'Receive my גט for me.' The agent told the husband, 'Your wife said: Receive my גט for me.' The husband answered 'bring', 'give to her', 'acquire for her', or 'receive for her.' If he wants to take it back, he cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. Its first opinion says that once the husband gives the גט to the wife's receiving agent, he cannot take it back, no matter which words he used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife made this person her receiving agent, so when he gets the גט, she is already divorced. The husband's words 'bring' or 'give' do not change that. Since the divorce has already happened, there is nothing left to take back.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught: this opens a ברייתא
Receive: the words that make someone a receiving agent
Bring/deliver: the words of a delivery agent
Acquire: take ownership on her behalf
To retract, to take back the גט

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"Receive my bill of divorce for me,"
and "Your wife said: Receive my bill of divorce for me,"
and he says: "Bring," and "Give to her,"
"Acquire for her," and "Receive for her" —
if he wants to retract, he cannot retract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new ברייתא about the husband's wording when the wife appointed a receiving agent.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once the wife appointed a שליח קבלה, the husband's wording does not matter. Handing over the גט divorces her right away, so he cannot retract.

steps.title: רבי נתן: 'bring and give' lets him take it back
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן splits the wordings. With 'bring and give' the husband can retract. With 'acquire' or 'receive' he cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: If he said 'bring and give to her', he may take it back. If he said 'acquire for her' or 'receive for her', he cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן disagrees with the first opinion. He says the husband's words do matter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'bring and give', the husband turns the agent into a שליח הולכה (delivery agent). Then the divorce happens only when the גט reaches her, so he can still take it back before that. 'Acquire' and 'receive' fit the receiving role, so the divorce happens right away.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion
A delivery agent: the divorce happens only when the גט reaches her
He may retract

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says:
"Bring and give to her" —
if he wants to retract, he may retract;
"Acquire for her" and "Receive for her" —
if he wants to retract, he cannot retract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion in the same ברייתא that disagrees with the first.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband's 'bring and give' turns the agent into a delivery agent, so he can retract. 'Acquire' or 'receive' does not, so he cannot.

steps.title: רבי: no taking back unless the husband clearly rejects the receiving role
steps.stepSummary: רבי says he cannot retract in all the cases. He can retract only if he says outright, 'I do not want you to receive for her; rather bring and give to her.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי says: In all of these cases, he cannot take it back. But if he told the agent, 'I do not want you to receive it for her, only bring it and give it to her,' then he may take it back.
steps.whatsHappening: A third opinion. רבי agrees that plain wording does not help the husband, but he adds a case where it does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Simply saying 'bring' is not enough to cancel the wife's appointment. Only a clear refusal of the receiving role turns the agent into a delivery agent. Then the husband can take the גט back before it reaches her.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי יהודה הנשיא
In all of them
I do not want, I refuse

phrases.english: Rabbi says:

phrases.aramaic: בְּכוּלָּן – אִם רָצָה לַחְזוֹר, לֹא יַחְזוֹר.
phrases.english: In all of them, if he wants to retract, he cannot retract.
phrases.notes: 'All of them' means all four wordings the husband might use.

phrases.english: But if he said to him:
"I do not want you to receive for her,
rather, bring and give to her,"
if he wants to retract, he may retract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third opinion in the ברייתא that adds an exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plain wording does not cancel the receiving role. Only a clear refusal ('I do not want you to receive') lets the husband retract.

steps.title: Isn't רבי saying the same thing as the first opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי's view is different from the תנא קמא. Both say he cannot retract in all the cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי is the same as the first תנא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רבי seems to repeat the first opinion. Why would the ברייתא list him as a separate view?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both say 'he cannot retract' for all four wordings. If they agree, there seems to be no reason to list רבי separately.

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi is the same as the first tanna!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the structure of the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: Listing רבי as a separate opinion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי and the תנא קמא give the same ruling for all the wordings, so there seems to be no disagreement.

steps.title: First answer: רבי comes to teach the 'I do not want' case
steps.stepSummary: רבי adds something new: a clear refusal does turn the agent into a delivery agent.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: he comes to teach us the case of 'I do not want.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי is adding a new case the first opinion never discussed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי may agree with the first opinion about the four wordings. His new point is that an outright refusal of the receiving role does work. Then the husband can retract.

keyTerms.meaning: If you want, say: this introduces one possible answer
He comes to teach us

phrases.english: If you want, say:
he comes to teach us the case of "I do not want";

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי adds nothing to the first opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי's new point is that 'I do not want you to receive' makes the agent a delivery agent.

steps.title: Second answer: the first opinion is רבי himself
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is telling us that the unnamed first opinion belongs to רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: this is what it teaches us: who is the first תנא? It is רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: A second answer. The repetition is there to show us that the first, unnamed opinion was רבי's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no disagreement between them at all. The ברייתא repeats the ruling in רבי's name to show us who the first opinion was, and then adds his explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us
Who

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא has three views: no retracting at all; רבי נתן, who lets the husband retract with 'bring and give'; and רבי, who lets him retract only with a clear 'I do not want you to receive.'

phrases.english: And if you want, say:
this is what it teaches us:
who is the first tanna? Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא: הָא קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי and the תנא קמא are two separate opinions.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are one opinion. The ברייתא is showing us that the first opinion was רבי's.

steps.title: For רבי נתן, is 'here you are' like 'acquire'?
steps.stepSummary: A question is raised: according to רבי נתן, if the husband says 'here you are', does it count like 'acquire' (no retracting) or not?
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: 'Here you are' — according to רבי נתן, is it like 'acquire', or is it not like 'acquire'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about a wording the ברייתא did not mention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי נתן, 'acquire' means the husband cannot retract, and 'bring and give' means he can. The question is which group 'here you are' belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: They asked: this opens an open question
Here you are, take it
Is similar to, counts like

phrases.english: They asked:
"Here you are" — according to Rabbi Natan,
is it like "acquire,"
or is it not like "acquire"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רבי נתן's view to ask about a new wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether, for רבי נתן, 'here you are' counts like 'acquire' (no retracting) or like 'bring' (retracting allowed).

steps.title: Quoting the משנה to try to answer the question
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a husband who says 'receive this גט for my wife' or 'deliver this גט to my wife' can still retract, but once a woman's own agent has received her גט, the husband cannot retract.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if a man says, 'Receive this גט for my wife,' or 'Deliver this גט to my wife,' and he wants to back out, he may back out. If a woman says, 'Receive my גט for me,' and the husband wants to back out after the agent receives it, he may not back out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the משנה as a possible source to answer the question about 'here you are' according to רבי נתן. This line only quotes the source; the inference from it comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sets up two kinds of agents. If the husband appoints the agent, even with the word 'receive,' the agent is just carrying the גט for him, so the husband can still cancel. If the wife appoints the agent, the agent's receiving counts as her receiving, so the divorce is done and the husband cannot retract. The גמרא hopes the exact wording the משנה lists will show how 'here you are' should be treated.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Come and hear.' The גמרא is bringing a source to try to answer the question.
'Receive.' Used here for appointing an agent to accept the גט.
'Deliver' or 'bring.' This appoints a delivery agent who carries the גט to the wife.
'He wants to retract,' meaning to back out of the divorce or cancel the agent.
'He may not retract.' The divorce has already taken effect.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the word הִתְקַבֵּל always means the divorce is final. When the husband says it, he can still retract. Only when the wife appoints the agent to receive does the divorce take effect once the agent gets it.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
phrases.notes: This tries to answer the question about 'here you are' from step 19.

phrases.english: One who says, 'Receive this גט for my wife'
or 'Deliver this גט to my wife,'
if he wants to retract, he may retract.
A woman who said, 'Receive my גט for me,'
if he wants to retract, he may not retract.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the husband, after he has handed the גט to the wife's agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts an attempted resolution of the question raised in step 19 by quoting the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: Whether, according to רבי נתן, the husband's words 'here you are' (הילך) count like 'acquire' (זכי), so that he cannot retract.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that contrasts a husband's agent ('receive' or 'deliver,' where he can retract) with a wife's receiving agent (where he cannot retract).
